How IPL Treatments Work

Face Skin & Body Bar in Calgary offers advanced IPL Treatments, using our powerful Lumecca IPL device. This is a highly effective solution for skin concerns related to the tone and texture of the skin. An IPL Treatment, or Intense Pulse Light, employs broad-spectrum pulsed light to precisely target specific chromophores (reds and browns) within the skin, namely, melanin (pigment) and hemoglobin (blood vessels). The pulsed light energy is absorbed by these targets in the skin, generating controlled thermal damage. This process effectively breaks down unwanted pigmentation that presents as age spots and sun damage, and coagulates the blood vessels that contribute to vascular lesions and redness. Our IPL Treatments using our Lumecca IPL are non-ablative, treating the dermal layers without disrupting the epidermal surface of the skin, resulting in a more even complexion and refined skin tone. The sophisticated technology of Intense Pulse Light allows our skilled practitioners to customize IPL Treatment parameters to directly address your individual skin concerns with optimal efficacy.
Benefits Of IPL Treatments

Choosing IPL Treatments at Face Skin & Body Bar yields significant benefits for achieving clearer, more youthful-looking skin. A primary outcome is the effective reduction of sun damage, as IPL Treatments precisely target and diminish age spots, sun spots, and hyperpigmentation, resulting in a more even complexion. For individuals experiencing redness and vascular lesions such as broken capillaries and rosacea, the Lumecca IPL can noticeably decrease their appearance, promoting a more balanced skin tone. Furthermore, Intense Pulse Light stimulates collagen production, leading to improved overall skin tone and texture, and a reduction in the appearance of fine lines. Regular IPL Treatments provide a comprehensive strategy for addressing multiple skin concerns and achieving substantial improvements in skin clarity and uniformity.

IPL treatments can effectively target any sun-exposed areas, such as the hands, arms, shoulders, upper back, neck, and décolleté area. This versatile treatment is also a valuable preventative measure against future pigmentation, with annual sessions working to address developing pigment and vascularity within the dermis.

blocks.text: BBL vs Lumecca: What’s the Difference?
blocks.html: BBL vs Lumecca: What’s the Difference?

While both treatments use advanced light energy to clear sun damage and redness, Lumecca is widely considered the most powerful IPL on the market today. While traditional BBL (BroadBand Light) is a fantastic tool for long-term skin maintenance and typically requires a series of 3-5 sessions, Lumecca delivers up to 3x more peak power to target pigment specifically. This means our Calgary clients often see results in fewer sessions when compared to BBL. If you are looking to erase years of sun damage or persistent rosacea with maximum efficiency and fewer trips to the clinic, Lumecca is our top recommendation.
Ideal Candidates

If you're looking to address sun damage, age spots, sun spots, uneven pigmentation, redness, rosacea, or visible vascular lesions, Intense Pulsed Light (IPL) therapy, including Lumecca IPL, could be your solution.

The most effective candidates for IPL are those with lighter skin tones, typically assessed as a Fitzpatrick Scale I, II, III, or very light IV, and those with minimal to no tan. This is crucial for achieving optimal results.

Often called 'laser season', these treatments are best during Calgary's colder, darker months (September to May) when limiting sun exposure is easier. It's an excellent annual treatment to repair summer sun damage and achieve a more even complexion with enhanced skin tone and texture.
Our experienced practitioners will conduct a thorough skin assessment during your consultation to determine if IPL is the right path for your desired outcomes.
IPL Pre-Treatment Checklist
To ensure the best results and the highest level of safety for your skin, please follow these guidelines before your session at Face Skin & Body Bar:

items: Avoid the Sun (4 Weeks Prior): This is the most important rule! Do not have a tan (natural or spray tan) on the treatment area. Lumecca targets pigment, and if your skin is tanned, the laser cannot distinguish between your tan and your sunspots, which increases the risk of a burn.
Stop Retinoids (7 Days Prior): Pause any Retin-A, Tretinoin, or high-strength Retinol products one week before your appointment, as these make the skin extra sensitive to light.
Check Your Medications: Some antibiotics and herbal supplements (like St. John’s Wort) cause photosensitivity. Please let us know if you have started any new medications recently.
No Waxing or Peels (2 Weeks Prior): Avoid any aggressive skin treatments, including chemical peels or waxing, in the area to be treated.

blocks.html: What To Expect From Treatment

Your IPL Treatment session at Face Skin & Body Bar in Calgary will be a carefully administered procedure focused on achieving optimal results. Protective eyewear will be provided. A cooling gel will be applied to the designated treatment area to ensure patient comfort and facilitate precise energy delivery. The Lumecca IPL device will be systematically applied to the treatment area, emitting controlled pulses of Intense Pulse Light. Patients may perceive a brief sensation of warmth or a mild snap during each pulse, which is generally well-tolerated. The duration of the IPL Treatments will be determined by the size of the treatment area and the specific skin concerns being addressed, typically ranging from 30 minutes to one hour.
Post-Treatment: What to Expect
Lumecca IPL is a powerful treatment, and your skin’s "healing journey" will depend on whether we targeted sun damage (pigment) or redness (vascularity). Here is the timeline for your results:

items: The First 24–48 Hours: Your skin will feel warm, similar to a mild sunburn. You may experience slight swelling or "puffiness," especially around the eyes and cheeks. This is a normal sign that the light energy has successfully reached its target.

For Sun Damage & Brown Spots: Over the next few days, your pigmented spots will darken and rise to the surface, looking like tiny coffee grounds. Do not scrub or pick at them! They will naturally flake off within 7–10 days, revealing a brighter, clearer complexion underneath.

For Redness, Rosacea & Veins: You may notice your skin looks slightly "flush" or that certain vessels turn a darker purple or grey before they fade. It is crucial to avoid heat (hot tubs, saunas, heavy exercise, and spicy foods) for 48 hours to allow the treated vessels to remain closed and heal properly.

Pro-Tip for Calgary Residents: Our high-altitude sun is intense! Always protect your investment with a physical SPF 30+ and a hat for at least two weeks post-treatment to prevent new pigment from forming.

Results And Recovery
Results

Following a series of IPL treatments at Face Skin & Body Bar, you can anticipate a progressive and noticeable improvement in your skin tone and overall complexion. Here's what you'll typically observe:
Pigmentation: Age spots and other pigmented lesions will initially darken before gradually fading as your body naturally eliminates the treated pigment.
Redness: You'll see a visible reduction in redness and superficial vascular lesions.
Texture and Fine Lines: The treatment stimulates collagen production, which contributes to enhanced skin texture and a diminished appearance of fine lines.
While you will see an immediate improvement in skin tone after the first week, your full results will continue to settle over 10–14 days.
Thanks to its advanced technology, Lumecca IPL often delivers particularly impactful results.

blocks.text: IPL Recovery Timeline: What To Expect
blocks.html: IPL Recovery Timeline: What To Expect
The recovery period after an IPL treatment is typically minimal, often just 5 to 12 hours of increased sensitivity and redness.

However, your individual recovery time can vary. If you have more severe rosacea or deeper pigmentation, your downtime might extend to several days, or even up to a week. The risk of bruising also increases with the severity of your concerns and individual skin characteristics.

Rest assured, all of this will be thoroughly discussed during your initial consultation and patch test. This way, you'll know exactly what to expect and can plan accordingly. We also progressively adjust treatment parameters to ensure you achieve the most optimal results. Your provider will give you a clear indication of your likely downtime based on your personalized assessment and treatment plan.

Patients may experience transient mild redness and a sensation of warmth in the treatment area, comparable to mild sun exposure, which generally resolves within half a day. Treated pigmented lesions may exhibit a temporary darkening and potential superficial flaking over 1 to 2 weeks. Strict adherence to sun protection, including consistent use of a broad-spectrum SPF 30 or higher, is essential. Routine skincare can typically be resumed immediately, with gentle care of the treated skin.
